result.summary: 30 cases cover all 19 functional requirements and all 4 non-functional requirements, including specified failure paths, abuse limits, response contracts, observability, and release gates.

test_cases.check: Request a pre-existing active link and verify the response is the existing 302 with the same Location and Cache-Control behavior; verify the stored destination is unchanged.
Verify existing expired and deleted link records retain their current 410 and 404 behavior across an application restart, and verify no migration changes the existing link or tombstone data.
Submit invalid create input and a conflicting alias; verify each returns its existing 400 or 409 status and exact existing error code.
Call stats and delete without a token and with an incorrect token below the limit; verify respectively 401/missing_token and 403/invalid_token.
Request unknown and deleted codes and an expired link; verify 404/not_found for the first two and 410/expired for the last.
Make the database link lookup fail during a redirect; verify 503/service_unavailable, Retry-After: 5, the standard JSON error body, and exactly one lookup attempt.
Cause an unexpected server exception; verify 500/internal_error with the standard JSON body and confirm the response contains no exception text, stack trace, or internal details.

Exercise application and framework errors, including unmatched route, unsupported method, oversized body, and unexpected exception; verify each has application/json and exactly the error and message fields with its specified status/code pair.
From one direct peer IP, create 20 links within a minute and verify they are admitted; verify the next create returns 429/rate_limited with a Retry-After header.

With a controlled clock, verify the limiter admits 10 supplied incorrect attempts per peer in a rolling 60-second window, blocks the next incorrect attempt with a positive delta-seconds retry time, and admits an attempt after the oldest blocking entry expires.

Make 10 incorrect-token requests distributed across stats and delete from one direct peer; verify the next incorrect request to either route returns 429/rate_limited with Retry-After. Verify missing-token requests return 401 without consuming attempts, a valid token is still processed at the limit, and spoofed forwarding headers do not change the peer identity.
Issue a sequence of unknown and deleted-code redirects from one peer; verify none is rate-limited and their metrics share one aggregate 404 outcome with no code or cause dimension.

Send /api/** bodies of exactly 16,384 and 16,385 actual bytes; verify the boundary-sized request is not rejected for size and the larger request returns 413/payload_too_large with the standard JSON body. Repeat with absent or inaccurate Content-Length to verify enforcement uses received bytes.

Inspect representative success, redirect, error, public health, and Actuator responses; verify all include X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, and Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'.

Generate redirect outcomes 302, 404, 410, and 5xx, then query local Actuator metrics; verify each outcome count and redirect timing are observable, and unknown/deleted 404s are aggregated without code- or cause-specific labels.

Verify the management listener is bound to 127.0.0.1 on its separate port, health and metrics are reachable locally, no other Actuator endpoint is exposed, and a request through the public listener cannot reach Actuator.
Request /health on the main port and verify its existing status and response body are unchanged.
Exercise successful and failed visitor redirects, then inspect captured application logs; verify the change emits no visitor-specific code, IP, destination, or request logging.

Redirect to a destination served by a recording test server and verify no outbound request is made; verify redirect handling performs no destination retry or reputation/malware lookup and introduces no authentication requirement beyond the existing management token.
Review the change manifest and build artifacts; verify changes are confined to the url-shortener service and introduce no infrastructure, deployment, or third-party integration changes.
With the service and database available, request active links repeatedly and verify every response is the expected successful redirect and none is 5xx.
Run the existing in-process redirect latency check and verify the measured p99 is below 50 ms.
Capture logs while exercising visitor requests and verify no new visitor-specific log entries or fields are emitted.
Run the complete existing and new automated test suite; verify all tests pass, the reported suite count is at least 95, and automated tests exercise the required security headers and error behavior.

decisions.choice: Verify existing records and tombstones across restart and verify no migration alters them; do not invent a time-based retention test.
decisions.rationale: The specification requires retention behavior to remain unchanged but provides no retention duration or expiry schedule that an automated test could assert.

decisions.choice: Run the existing in-process p99 check as the automated gate.
decisions.rationale: Results can vary with the test environment; this is the closest specified automated check, but it does not establish production latency under all deployment conditions.

decisions.choice: Verify loopback binding and test that the public listener cannot access management endpoints.
decisions.rationale: The test environment may not provide a separate external network host; the listener binding and public-interface behavior are the closest meaningful automated checks.

decisions.choice: Inspect captured logs for visitor-specific information while exercising representative requests.
decisions.rationale: Automated tests can check observed logs but cannot prove the absence of such logging on every future execution path.

decisions.choice: Use a change-manifest and artifact review rather than a runtime behavior test.
decisions.rationale: Whether infrastructure, deployment, or third-party changes occurred is a repository and delivery-scope property, not a service behavior that can be proven through HTTP tests.

decisions.choice: Track product-owner approval as a release checklist gate outside the automated test suite.
decisions.rationale: Approval is a human decision and cannot be established by an automated test.
